items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: Like what Frankie Avalon did in some of his video clips.

ctx.x: Would you think, would all those dominoes have started and fallen into place if you hadn’t been a player first? And what I mean by that is sometimes I’m fascinated by people who are tremendous fans of the music or they make a living as perhaps a jazz journalists but they weren’t players first. So did your trumpet playing lead to all these things? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Great question, and I did think about that. I’ll be honest with you I thought about that before this interview. I’ve been truly, truly blessed to come from a family, not so much of musicians although there were some, two of the paternal great, great, great whatever back in Italy were bandmasters. And when I was a youngster at about five years old one of my uncles was a student of Doc Cheatham. He was a semi-pro trumpet player. But here’s the thing. There was always pervasive music in the household, predominantly…
